thesis_he.bear: SpaceX עם שיגורים ותדרים משלה תופסת את שוק הסלולר מהחלל, המיזם המשותף של AT&T/Verizon/T-Mobile מוריד את חלקה של ASTS בהכנסות, והפריסה ממשיכה להתעכב ולדרוש עוד גיוסי הון.
thesis_he.base: השוק גדל, ASTS מגיעה לכ-45 לוויינים בתחילת 2027 ומתחילה הכנסות שירות דרך AT&T, Verizon ו-Vodafone כספק שני לצד SpaceX, אבל בלי יתרון ברור ובחלוקת הכנסות שלא פורסמה.
thesis_he.bull: ASTS מוכיחה פס רחב לטלפון רגיל בעומס מסחרי, מגיעה ל-90 לוויינים, והמפעילים הגדולים (מחוץ ל-T-Mobile) מעבירים אליה תעבורה ותדרים, כך שהיא הופכת לספק המועדף שלהם מול SpaceX.

market_direction.reading: The direct-to-device market is growing, but its size is very uncertain. Omdia (2026-03-02) projects about $12bn of smartphone D2D service revenue and 411m monthly users by 2030 and expects cellular-standard devices (Starlink D2C, AST SpaceMobile) to be over 95% of D2D users. The leading competitor's filings confirm paid demand: SpaceX's Enterprise & Government revenue, which includes Starlink Mobile, was $5.04bn in 9M 2026 (+70%). ASTS has signed 60+ MNOs covering 3bn+ subscribers (commitments, not paid usage), and AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon formed a D2D joint venture on 2026-10-02. Other studies seen only as undated excerpts range from $2.6bn to $28bn, so market size is a warning row, not a driver.

bottleneck_potential.reading: ASTS can become a capacity bottleneck only once it has satellites in orbit. Its large-array BlueBirds deliver broadband to unmodified phones over MNO spectrum, but supply today is 13 satellites (2026-08-10) against guidance of about 45 in early 2027 (slipped from 45-60 by end-2026) and about 90 for the funded Block 2 build. Capacity is gated by launch access and build rate (up to 6 satellites a month of assembly capacity; 10 launches booked with two providers), not by demand. SpaceX adds D2D capacity faster with its own rockets and its own EchoStar AWS-4/H-block spectrum (FCC approved 2026-05-12), so any scarcity value for ASTS is limited to MNOs that want a second supplier (AT&T, Verizon, Vodafone via SatCo).

share_trajectory.reading: On numbers, SpaceX (SPCX) is taking the D2D share now: its Enterprise & Government revenue including Starlink Mobile was $5.04bn in 9M 2026 (+70%; Q3 +91%) and T-Mobile's service is live. ASTS has recognized no SpaceMobile service revenue; its H1 2026 revenue of $46.2m is $37.8m gateway products (near cost) plus $8.4m mostly U.S. Government services. Legacy MSS names grow slowly: Iridium (IRDM) +4.8% in 9M 2026 with operating margin down to 16.9% from 27.4%, Globalstar (GSAT) +6.0% in H1 2026, Viasat/Inmarsat (VSAT) -1.2% in its June 2026 quarter. None shows a loss to ASTS yet because ASTS is not in service; ASTS's share is a future question decided by deployment.

competitive_position.reading: Against SpaceX (SPCX) ASTS is weaker on everything that exists today: satellites in orbit (13 vs over 11,000 Starlink), launch (none owned vs owned), spectrum (MNO leases plus pending Ligado L-band, $520m paid and refundable only if approvals fail, vs owned EchoStar AWS-4/H-block) and paid service (zero vs live). It is stronger on carrier contracts outside T-Mobile (AT&T, Verizon, Vodafone/SatCo) and on claimed broadband per beam from its large arrays (Block 1 demonstrated broadband to unmodified phones). Against Iridium, Globalstar and Viasat/Inmarsat, ASTS targets broadband to ordinary phones versus their low-data messaging and voice, but it has no service revenue base yet.

threats.reading: 1) Substitution by SpaceX Starlink D2C, which owns launch and now its own mobile spectrum. 2) Channel power: the AT&T/T-Mobile/Verizon D2D joint venture (2026-10-02) could standardize wholesale terms and compress ASTS's undisclosed revenue share. 3) Launch dependence: BB7 was lost at launch (Q2 2026 write-off $125.9m) and deployment guidance slipped twice to about 45 satellites in early 2027. 4) Regulation: Ligado L-band rights ($520m paid) and SCS licences granted only in part. 5) Funding and dilution: about $3.70bn of convertibles (incl. $1.15bn 2034 notes issued July 2026), H1 2026 capex $859m, and diluted shares up from 81.8m (FY2023) to 299.1m (Q2 2026).

moat.note: Against SpaceX: contracts with 60+ MNOs and leased spectrum exist, but there is no service revenue or return on capital to show a moat; SpaceX competes directly with its own spectrum and launch.

pricing_power.note: Revenue share with MNOs is not disclosed; the carriers' joint venture (2026-10-02) strengthens the buyers' side. Gateway products sell near cost (Q2 2026 products revenue $24.4m vs cost $22.4m).

customer_concentration.note: All H1 2026 revenue came from gateway sales to a handful of MNOs (13 gateways to 7 customers) and U.S. Government milestones; per-customer percentages were not located this run (gap).

market_size.note: One attributed study (Omdia ~$12bn by 2030) plus SpaceX's fast-growing E&G segment show a real paid market; size is highly uncertain (other excerpts $2.6-28bn).

competition.note: SpaceX Starlink D2C is ahead commercially (T-Mobile live), owns launch and spectrum; carriers formed a joint D2D venture that negotiates collectively.

capital_allocation.note: Diluted shares rose about 3.7x since FY2023; $89.8m induced conversion expense and $118.8m SBC in H1 2026 (SBC 2.6x revenue); no buybacks. Cash and restricted cash $2.7bn at 2026-06-30 includes $434.6m restricted (not spendable); the July 2026 $1.15bn notes add to it. Management says the ~90-satellite build is fully funded.

management.note: Revenue guidance met once (H2 2025 $69.0m vs $50-75m), but deployment slipped twice (45-60 by end-2026 to ~45 in early 2027) and opex guidance was raised from $70-80m to about $100m a quarter.

governance.note: The CEO controls the vote through 78.2m Class C super-voting shares; a senior-management change-of-control severance policy was adopted (8-K 2026-09-28).

regulation.note: SCS licences granted in part / deferred in part; Ligado L-band approvals pending ($520m paid, refundable only if they fail); Sound Point facility status after 2026-08-10 unconfirmed.

technology_ai.note: Block 1 demonstrated broadband to unmodified phones; not yet proven at commercial load or at Block 2 scale.

geopolitics.note: Israel operations are ~1% of assets and ~5% of opex (6M 2026), not materially affected per the 10-Q; tariff exposure on satellite parts is unsized.

gaps: Outside view (warning only, sets no number): pre-revenue satellite constellations historically often needed restructuring or heavy dilution before service scale.
